newsitem.title: UK: IBCA studies state support for German Landesbanks.
newsitem.headline: IBCA studies state support for German Landesbanks.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday that it was studying the future of state support for Germany's Landesbanks.

In a report on the legal background to the current deliberations between the European Commission and the differing factions within the German banking sector, IBCA said it expected that over the long-term, Landesbanks would be privatised, with their creditors being provided with adequate information on when and if the state guarantee is to be removed.
"The market is an impatient master and may not be prepared to wait." IBCA said in a statement.

"Meanwhile, all participants should now realise that the arcane arguments of lawyers and regulators in regard to the Anstaltslast and Gewaehrtraegerhaftung system can no longer be swept under the carpet as the irrelevant and incomprehensible mitherings of academics and feuding bankers," it added.
IBCA said that the German private-law bankers' association had already taken the issue to the Commission.

The association was arguing that the current system of state support -- the Anstaltslast and Gewaehrtraegerhaftung system - allows Landesbanks to be provided with capital backing which is anti-competitive and thereby an infringement of EU law.

"Meanwhile, Karel van Miert, the European Commissioner in charge of Directorate-General IV (DG IV) which has responsibility for competition, has made clear his opposition in principle to this system of support," the report said.
describing the issue as "politically charged", the report also noted that German Chancellor Helmut Kohl had publicly stated his support for the status quo.
"It is difficult to predict the outcome," IBCA said.
Bu it added that banking guarantee system which "evolved in pre-1871 Prussia, while doubtless appropriate to the needs of the time, is unlikely to be relevant or suitable today".
IBCA stressed that change was likely to be slow and current holders of Landesbank debt would continue to benefit from state support/guarantees even if change did occur.
"IBCA has not changed the ratings of any of the public-law banks it rates which, because of the support system, have all been assigned AAA long-term ratings," the report said.
